newsitem.title: CHINA: Taiwan has capacity to cause U.S.-China conflict.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan has capacity to cause U.S.-China conflict.

text.p: Barber Conable, chairman of the U.S. National Committee on U.S.-China Relations warned on Sunday that the Taiwan issue still had the capacity to bring the two countries into "tragic and unnecessary conflict".

Conable was addressing a dinner to mark the 25th anniversary of the signing of the Shanghai Communique which established a basis for the eventual establishment of diplomatic ties between Beijing and Washington in 1979.

In the communique, the United States acknowledged that there was only one China, but made no comment on its capital or rightful government, hotly contested between Beijing and the Nationalist government in Taipei.
Conable said the communique's wording on the Taiwan question was still relevant today.

"The Communique correctly asserted that (Taiwan) is an issue that must be handled with the utmost sensitivity and mutual restraint. This remains the principal issue that could bring American and China into tragic and unnecesaary conflict," he said.
"That was true in 1972 and it is, as events in 1995-96 revealed, true today as well," he added.

Relations between China and the U.S. fell to a new low last year over a number of issues, including Taiwan, with China putting pressure through missile tests and other means on Taiwan in the lead-up to the presidential elections in March, 1996.
Conable noted the huge increase in contacts of all kinds and at all levels between China and the United States that had occurred since 1972, adding:
"In the normal day-to-day frictions that beset the relations between our two great nations, we often lose sight of this progress and the importance of the principles which made those gains possible."

"Some of the conflicts we see today reflect past successes and the growth in the size and number of our interests, many of which are shared. Ironically, dealing with multipylying friction seems to be the price of overall progress amid greater interaction," he added.
